text:
Tom Willander came back into the Canucks' lineup on Friday against the Rangers, after almost two weeks out, and his first period back was the best case for him in a while. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis called it "Impressive first period from the Willander-Pettersson pairing, heavily tilting the ice at 5-on-5," and David Quadrelli of The Nation Network posted that chances were 14-1 for Vancouver with Willander on the ice in that period, per Natural Stat Trick. The Canucks still lost.

The 21-year-old, the 11th pick in 2023, plays about 20 minutes a night, and the points have dried up: none in 14 straight games. Our numbers say that is mostly bad luck, since his on-ice chances in that stretch were worth about 4.0 expected points (points the quality of chances would usually produce). At five on five Vancouver's share of expected goals is more than eight points higher with him on the ice than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season but also stuck with weaker teammates than almost anyone. He is also among the fastest skaters in the league by top speed (92nd percentile).
headline: Tom Willander's return shows the play behind the drought
